Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G
A
No disciplines have seized on professionalism with as much enthusiasm the humanities. You can, Mr. Menand points out, became a lawyer in three years and a medical doctor in four. But the regular time it takes to get a doctoral degree in the humanities is nine years. Not surprisingly, up to half of all doctoral students in English drop out before getting their degrees.
没有任何学科像人文学科那样热衷于专业化。梅南德先生指出，你可以三年成为律师、四年成为医生，但人文学科拿博士学位通常要九年。无怪乎多达一半的英语专业博士生在拿到学位前就辍学了。
B
His concern is mainly with the humanities: Literature, languages, philosophy and so on. These are disciplines that are going out of style: 22% of American college graduates now major in business compared with only 2% in history and 4% in English. However, many leading American universities want their undergraduates to have a grounding in the basic canon of ideas that every educated person should possess. 三段式：①描述图画（游客乱丢垃圾污染景区）；②阐释寓意（旅游中破坏环境的行为，讽刺只顾自己不顾环境的不文明现象）；③评论（应提高环保意识、文明旅游）。160-200词。

source_blocks.html:
参考范文

The thought-provoking picture depicts a boat drifting down a river, where sightseers casually toss litter overboard. The water is already littered with lunch boxes, bottles and waste paper, and the caption reads: the "leftovers" of a journey.

What the drawing exposes is a widespread malaise: while enjoying nature's beauty, many travelers leave behind a trail of damage. The "leftovers" in the caption refer not to food, but to the garbage and pollution thoughtless tourists abandon in their wake. Such behavior not only spoils the charm of scenic spots but also wrecks the ecosystem, turning a pleasant trip into an environmental tragedy.

From my perspective, urgent action is called for. First, tourists should be educated to raise their environmental awareness and behave responsibly. Second, scenic areas ought to tighten supervision and penalize littering. Only when every traveler treats nature with respect can we preserve the planet's beauty for generations to come.

【译文】

这幅发人深省的图画描绘了一艘在河上漂流的游船，游客随手将垃圾抛入水中。水面早已散落着饭盒、瓶子和废纸，图题写道：旅程之"余"。

画面所揭示的是一种普遍弊病：许多游客在享受自然之美的同时，却留下了一路破坏。标题中的"余"指的并非食物，而是无知游客抛在身后的垃圾与污染。这种行为不仅破坏了景区的魅力，更摧毁了生态环境，把一次愉快的旅程变成一场环境悲剧。

在我看来，亟需采取行动。首先，应教育游客增强环保意识、规范自身行为；其次，景区应加强监管并对乱扔垃圾者予以处罚。唯有每位游客都敬畏自然，我们才能为子孙后代留住这片美丽。

paragraphs.html: When Liam McGee departed as president of Bank of America in August, his explanation was surprisingly straight up. paragraphs.html: It's no surprise that Jennifer Senior's insightful, provocative magazine cover story, "I Love My Children, I Hate My Life," is arousing much chatter—nothing gets people talking like the suggestion that child rearing is anything less than a completely fulfilling, life-enriching experience. Rather than concluding that children make parents either happy or miserable, Senior suggests we need to redefine happiness: instead of thinking of it as something that can be measured by moment-to-moment joy, we should consider being happy as a past-tense condition. Even though the day-to-day experience of raising kids can be soul-crushingly hard, Senior writes that "the very things that in the moment dampen our moods can later be sources of intense gratification and delight."

No shock there, considering how much work it is to raise a kid without a partner to lean on; yet to hear Sandra and Britney tell it, raising a kid on their "own" (read: with round-the-clock help) is a piece of cake. 当然，《我们周刊》和《人物》等名人杂志所呈现的为人父母的形象极不现实，尤其是当父母是布洛克这样的单身母亲时。几项研究得出结论：有孩子的父母不如无子女的夫妻幸福，而单亲家庭最不幸福。这并不令人意外，想想在没有伴侣可以依靠的情况下养一个孩子有多辛苦；但听听桑德拉和布兰妮的说法吧，"独自"养孩子（实际意思是：有全天候帮手）简直是小菜一碟。 It's hard to imagine that many people are dumb enough to want children just because Reese and Angelina make it look so glamorous: most adults understand that a baby is not a haircut. But it's interesting to wonder if the images we see every week of stress-free, happiness-enhancing parenthood aren't in some small, subconscious way contributing to our own dissatisfactions with the actual experience, in the same way that a small part of us hoped getting "the Rachel" might make us look just a little bit like Jennifer Aniston. 很难想象，会有很多人蠢到仅仅因为瑞茜和安吉丽娜把养孩子这件事显得如此光鲜就想要孩子：大多数成年人都明白，养孩子不是剪个头发。但有趣的是，我们每周看到的那些无忧无虑、幸福感爆棚的为人父母形象，是否正以某种微小的、潜意识的方式加剧着我们对真实育儿经历的不满——就像我们内心一小部分人曾希望剪个"瑞秋头"能让自己看起来有点像詹妮弗·安妮斯顿一样。

partb_options.head: Part B 选项原文（英汉对照）A–G

options.label: A
options.en: No disciplines have seized on professionalism with as much enthusiasm the humanities. You can, Mr. Menand points out, became a lawyer in three years and a medical doctor in four. But the regular time it takes to get a doctoral degree in the humanities is nine years. Not surprisingly, up to half of all doctoral students in English drop out before getting their degrees.
options.zh: 没有任何学科像人文学科那样热衷于专业化。梅南德先生指出，你可以三年成为律师、四年成为医生，但人文学科拿博士学位通常要九年。无怪乎多达一半的英语专业博士生在拿到学位前就辍学了。

options.label: B
options.en: His concern is mainly with the humanities: Literature, languages, philosophy and so on. These are disciplines that are going out of style: 22% of American college graduates now major in business compared with only 2% in history and 4% in English. However, many leading American universities want their undergraduates to have a grounding in the basic canon of ideas that every educated person should possess. But most find it difficult to agree on what a "general education" should look like. At Harvard, Mr. Menand notes, "the great books are read because they have been read", they form a sort of social glue.
options.zh: 他主要关切的是人文学科：文学、语言、哲学等等。这些学科正日渐式微：如今22%的美国大学毕业生主修商科，而主修历史和英语的分别只有2%和4%。然而，许多美国顶尖大学希望本科生掌握每个受过教育的人都应具备的基本思想经典。但大多数学者难以就"通识教育"应有的模样达成一致。梅南德先生指出，在哈佛，"伟大著作之所以被读，是因为它们一直被读"，它们构成了某种社会黏合剂。

options.label: C
options.en: Equally unsurprisingly, only about half end up with professorships for which they entered graduate school. There are simply too few posts. This is partly because universities continue to produce ever more PhDs. But fewer students want to study humanities subjects: English department awarded more bachelor's degrees in 1970-71 than they did 20 years later. Fewer students requires fewer teachers. So, at the end of a decade of theses-writing, many humanities students leave the profession to do something for which they have not been trained.
options.zh: 同样不意外的是，最终只有约一半人获得了他们读研所瞄准的教授职位。实在是因为岗位太少。这 partly 是因为大学仍在不断培养越来越多的博士。但愿意攻读人文学科的学生变少了：英语系在1970—71年授予的学士学位比20年后还要多。学生少了，教师需求也就少了。于是，在长达十年的论文写作之后，许多人文学生离开了本行，去做一些他们并未受过训练的工作。

options.label: D
options.en: One reason why it is hard to design and teach courses is that they can cut across the insistence by top American universities that liberal-arts educations and professional education should be kept separate, taught in different schools. Many students experience both varieties. Although more than half of Harvard undergraduates end up in law, medicine or business, future doctors and lawyers must study a non-specialist liberal-art degree before embarking on a professional qualification.
options.zh: 课程难以设计与讲授的一个原因是，它们会与顶尖美国大学所坚持的"文科教育与职业教育应当分离、分属不同学院"相冲突。许多学生两种都经历过。尽管超过半数的哈佛本科生最终进入法律、医学或商界，但未来的医生和律师在攻读职业资格之前，必须先修一个非专业性的文科学位。

options.label: E
options.en: Besides professionalizing the professions by this separation top American universities have professionalized the professor. The growth on public money for academic research has speeded the process: federal research grants rose fourfold between 1960 and 1990, but faculty teaching hours fell by half as research took its toll. Professionalism has turned the acquisition of a doctoral degree into a prerequisite for a successful academic career: as late as 1969 a third of American professors did not possess one. But the key idea behind professionalization, argues Mr. Menand, is that "the knowledge and skills needed for a particular specialization are transmissible but not transferable." So disciplines acquire a monopoly not just over the production of knowledge, but also over the production of the producers of knowledge.
options.zh: 除了通过这种分离使各职业专业化之外，顶尖美国大学还使教授这一职业本身专业化了。公共科研经费的增长加速了这一进程：1960至1990年间联邦研究资助增至四倍，但随着科研挤占，教师授课时数减半。专业化已把获得博士学位变成了学术生涯成功的前提：迟至1969年，仍有三分之一的美国教授没有博士学位。但梅南德先生认为，专业化背后的核心理念是"某一特定专业所需的知识和技能可以传授却不可转移"。于是学科不仅垄断了知识的生产，也垄断了知识生产者的生产。

options.label: F
options.en: The key to reforming higher education, concludes Mr. Menand, is to alter the way in which "the producers of knowledge are produced." Otherwise, academics will continue to think dangerously alike, increasingly detached from the societies which they study, investigate and criticize. "Academic inquiry, at least in some fields, may need to become less exclusionary and more holistic." Yet quite how that happens, Mr. Menand does not say.
options.zh: 梅南德先生总结道，改革高等教育的关键在于改变"知识生产者被生产出来的方式"。否则，学者们将继续危险地趋同思维，越来越脱离他们所研究、调查和批评的社会。"学术研究，至少在某些领域，或许需要变得少些排他、多些整体。"然而究竟如何做到，梅南德先生并未言明。

options.label: G
options.en: The subtle and intelligent little book The Marketplace of Ideas: Reform and Resistance in the American University should be read by every student thinking of applying to take a doctoral degree. They may then decide to go elsewhere. For something curious has been happening in American Universities, and Louis Menand, a professor of English at Harvard University, captured it skillfully.
options.zh: 这本精妙而睿智的小书《思想的市场：美国大学的改革与阻力》应当被每一个考虑申请攻读博士学位的学生阅读。他们读后或许会决定另谋出路。因为美国大学里正发生着某种怪事，而哈佛英语教授路易斯·梅南德巧妙地捕捉到了它。
